gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the makers' call-time ratings are much lower than the music-playback numbers the rival pages quote: Jabra rates the Evolve3 85 at 55 h for music but only 21 h of talk time with ANC and busylight on, and Sony rates the WH-1000XM6 at 24 h of talk time with NC on, so on calls the Sony is rated to last longer than the Jabra, the reverse of what the 55 h vs 30 h headlines suggest.
standout_why: SoundGuys' 'best noise canceling headphones for work' page (cited in both chats) gives the Jabra Evolve3 85 as 'up to 55 hours with ANC on' and the Sony WH-1000XM6 as 'Sony rates 30 hours with ANC on' plus a 37 h 14 min lab test. These are all music-playback figures, and the page gives no talk-time number for any pick. SoundGuys' 'best headphones with mic for conference calls' page gives no talk-time figure for any product either. I could not compare against the cited RTINGS page or the cited What Hi-Fi page because neither returned its article body to the fetcher. RTINGS publishes measured playback battery life, not talk time, but I did not confirm that on this page.
decides: For someone buying headphones mainly for calls, this backs ChatGPT's 'Sony WH-1000XM6 best overall' pick and undercuts the main reason to pay more for the Jabra Evolve3 85 as the 'work' choice. On the makers' own call ratings the Sony gets 24 h with NC on and the Jabra 21 h with ANC and busylight on. The Jabra's 55 h is a music figure, and talk time is 38% of it. The Sony's talk time is 80% of its 30 h music rating. Among the budget options, the Soundcore Space 2 Pro (which Dealectric lists) is the only Soundcore model whose US page states a talk time: 20 h, against 30 h of music with ANC on. The Space Q45 that ChatGPT showed states no talk time and is listed as out of stock on Soundcore's US store. Every rated talk time here is at least 20 h, so any of them covers a single workday of calls. The finding changes which one wins on longevity across several days of calls, not whether one makes it through a day.
